sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Alnus glutinosa is a deciduous tree reaching about 25 m. Its rounded leaves are often notched at the tip. Long, hanging male catkins appear alongside smaller female catkins, which mature into woody, cone-like structures about 2 cm long. It prefers wet soils, including riverbanks and marshes, and is native to Europe, North Africa and western Asia.

sections.title: Identification
sections.text: The woody female structures look like small cones, but alder is a broadleaf tree in the birch family, Betulaceae, not a conifer. Food use and toxicity are not established in the sources consulted.
